decisions.reason: The unscoped MS15202P claim omits the 5.8L application and the catalog row carries a VIN-N restriction that the public vehicle context cannot enforce.

sourceEvidence.title: Intake Manifold Gasket and EGR Tube Failures (Vacuum/Coolant Leaks)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the leaking intake manifold gasket (and clean sealing surfaces). For EGR faults, replace the cracked EGR tube and/or EGR valve (often requires pulling the intake plenum for access) and inspect the DPFE sensor and vacuum lines; clear carbon from EGR passages. Confirm the repair by verifying vacuum and rechecking for stored EGR codes.

decisions.reason: The unscoped 43186WT claim is cataloged for a different engine application than the article's 2.0L failure and covers only part of the article's years.

sourceEvidence.title: 2.0L EcoBoost Water Pump Failure and Coolant Leak
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the water pump. Due to the internal location, this is a major repair requiring timing cover removal — labor is 8-12 hours. Parts cost $150-300 for the pump plus timing chain components. Total repair: $1,500-3,000 at an independent shop. If coolant has mixed with oil, the engine may need additional flushing or repair. Monitor oil color — milky oil indicates coolant contamination. Change oil more frequently and check coolant level regularly.

decisions.reason: The unscoped Continental 40194 claim covers only the 1.9L application through 1996 and does not cover either 2.0L application or the full article range.

sourceEvidence.title: Timing belt is an age/interval wear item that can strand the car
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the timing belt on schedule (and any belt of unknown age on a used purchase), ideally together with the tensioner and water pump since the pump is driven off the same area. Use the correct Zetec cam-alignment tooling when doing the DOHC engine so the cams are timed correctly on reassembly.

decisions.reason: SKF BR930420 is a front 4WD hub application; the current unscoped two-vendor claim does not preserve the drivetrain and position restrictions needed for safe display.

sourceEvidence.title: Front Wheel Hub and Bearing Assembly Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the hub and bearing assembly. Use premium bearings rated for heavy-duty applications. Torque to spec (175 ft-lbs axle nut).

decisions.reason: The unscoped GN10237 row is cataloged for naturally aspirated applications and conflicts with the article's EcoBoost repair scope.

sourceEvidence.title: 3.5L EcoBoost Ignition Coil and Spark Plug Misfire (Often Caused by Broken Exhaust Manifold Studs)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace all six spark plugs with the updated Motorcraft SP-580 (supersedes SP-534, pre-gapped to ~0.032 in) and renew failed coil-on-plug units; do plugs as a set on or before the 60,000-100,000 mi interval (severe-duty/towing service much sooner). If misfires recur after coil/plug replacement, inspect for broken exhaust manifold studs/bolts and an exhaust leak at the head and replace the studs. Adding a catch can and the updated SP-580 plug reduces fouling on pre-2018 (DI-only) engines.

decisions.reason: Walker 235-1027 carries VIN, production-date, and market restrictions that are not represented by the unscoped public claim.

sourceEvidence.title: 4.0L SOHC Camshaft Position Sensor and Synchronizer Failure Causing P0340 Misfire and Stalling
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the camshaft synchronizer AND the camshaft position sensor as a set (do not reuse an old synchronizer with a new sensor). The synchronizer must be installed with a special alignment/synchronizer positioning tool (Ford 303-589 / equivalent) so the sensor vane is clocked correctly, or the engine will run poorly or throw the code again. Verify oil pump drive engagement and confirm no plastic debris fell into the timing area.

decisions.reason: The legacy 221-9025 row is unscoped and misses a 4.0L article year; the corrected packet introduces only the independently reviewed engine/year variants.

sourceEvidence.title: Internal Radiator Transmission Cooler Rupture Causing Coolant/ATF Cross-Contamination ('Pink Milkshake')
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the radiator with a new unit (and inspect/replace the cooler lines). If coolant reached the transmission, flush the cooling system AND service the transmission immediately — drop the pan, replace fluid and filter, and flush the cooler circuit; heavy contamination requires a rebuild. Many owners bypass the internal cooler and install an external transmission cooler to prevent recurrence.

decisions.component: Wheel Bearing and Hub Assembly Repair Kit
decisions.reason: SKF BR930259K carries a bearing-identification restriction that is absent from the article and cannot be enforced by the current vehicle selection.

sourceEvidence.title: Rear Wheel Bearing and Hub Failure Causing Growling Noise and ABS Concerns
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Diagnosis involves road testing for speed-related growl, checking for wheel play, and isolating the noisy corner with chassis ears or by loading the vehicle in turns. Repair is replacement of the affected hub/bearing assembly, and many owners replace both rear sides if mileage is high. Alignment and inspection of tires and rear suspension components are recommended afterward to rule out other noise sources.

decisions.reason: Bosch 0221504704 is unscoped across a broad F-150 year and engine range and lacks complete catalog coverage for the article.

sourceEvidence.title: Coil-On-Plug (COP) Ignition Coil Failure — Misfire and Rough Idle (Triton V8)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Confirm the bad coil by swapping it to an adjacent cylinder and seeing if the misfire follows. Replace the failed coil (and its spark plug), apply dielectric grease to the boot to seal out moisture. If the same cylinder fails repeatedly, replace the valve-cover gasket and clean oil from the plug tube. Consider a full coil/plug set at high mileage.

decisions.reason: MAHLE MS19261 is limited by engine, VIN, and year application while the existing public claim is unscoped.

sourceEvidence.title: Exhaust Manifold Studs / Bolts Break — Exhaust Leak and Cold-Start Ticking
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Confirm the leak (cold-start tick, soot/black streaking at the manifold flange). Replace broken studs/bolts with a hardware kit using anti-seize; studs snapped flush must be drilled out with a left-hand cobalt bit (often a 90-degree drill) and may require an EZ-out or, worst case, head removal. Inspect/replace the manifold gasket. Common parts: Dorman exhaust manifold hardware kits 03408 (gas V8) and 03430 (4.6/5.4 3V) plus OEM studs. Hardware $20-$60; professional repair commonly $300-$700, more if studs break flush or the manifold is cracked.

decisions.reason: MOOG 81118 has no complete catalog evidence for the article's vehicle scope, so the unscoped verified link cannot be retained.

sourceEvidence.title: Front Coil Spring Fractures from Corrosion — Snaps and Punctures Front Tire (11th-Gen Salt-Belt)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace both front coil springs (they are a matched pair) — corrosion-resistant/coated replacement springs are recommended. Inspect the shock/strut perch and lower control arm for damage from a spring that has already migrated. In the rust belt, coat new springs and inspect at every tire rotation. Any inner-edge tire scalloping on a truck that hasn't been aligned warrants a spring inspection.

decisions.reason: SKF BR931016 is not supported across the article's full application set and the current unscoped row loses drivetrain and hub-option restrictions.

sourceEvidence.title: Front Wheel Hub Bearing Assembly Failure — Humming Noise and ABS Light
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Confirm by checking for wheel-bearing play and locating the noise (worsens with speed, may change when loading the bearing in a turn). On 4WD, rule out IWE failure first (IWE grind often stops when 4WD is engaged; hub noise does not). Replace the complete hub/bearing assembly (bearing is not separately serviceable) and clear ABS codes. Torque axle nut and fasteners to spec.

decisions.reason: Bosch 6747 does not cover the article's 1998 endpoint and carries application variants that are absent from the unscoped claim.

sourceEvidence.title: Spark Plug Thread Blowout
sourceEvidence.howToFix: If not yet blown out: Use anti-seize compound on spark plug threads, torque to spec (11-15 ft-lbs), and change plugs every 30k miles. If blown out: Install a Helicoil or Time-Sert thread repair kit ($50-150 DIY, $150-500 at shop). Preventive repair kits are also available to reinforce threads before failure.

decisions.reason: Dayco DP2263 lacks catalog support for the article's 2021 endpoint, so the unscoped verified row is incomplete.

sourceEvidence.title: Water Pump Leak/Failure (3.5L EcoBoost)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace water pump when symptoms appear. Consider timing chain inspection/replacement at same time if high mileage. Replace thermostat while accessible. Ensure proper cooling system bleeding after repair.

decisions.reason: The Sachs K70564-01 claim conflicts with the DPS6 repair application and lacks the transmission-specific scope needed to distinguish it from manual and ST applications.

sourceEvidence.title: DPS6 PowerShift Dual-Clutch Transmission Shudder, Slipping, and Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Check if your vehicle is covered under Ford's extended warranty or class-action settlement — many Fiestas qualify for free clutch and TCM replacement. If out of warranty, have the clutch assembly and TCM reprogrammed or replaced ($1,500-$3,500). Some owners have had success with multiple TCM reflashes to improve shift quality. As a last resort, some owners have converted to a manual transmission. Avoid the PowerShift entirely when purchasing a used Fiesta — manual transmission models are far more reliable.

decisions.reason: SKF BR930704 is a rear AWD application without the sensor configuration described by the article, while the existing row is unscoped and presented as a front repair.

sourceEvidence.title: Front Wheel Bearing Hub Assembly Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the hub and bearing assembly. The ABS sensor is integrated, so the tone ring alignment is automatic with a new assembly. Torque the axle nut to 233 ft-lbs.

decisions.reason: The unscoped WPFD-609V row covers only a subset of the article's years and carries engine/application restrictions that are not enforced publicly.

sourceEvidence.title: Internal Water Pump Failure Causes Coolant-Oil Mixing and Catastrophic Engine Damage
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Proactively replace the water pump and timing chain as preventive maintenance between 100,000-120,000 miles ($1,500-$2,500 labor-intensive job). Check oil regularly for milky appearance or coolant smell — catching it early can save the engine. If coolant is found in the oil, stop driving immediately and have it towed. Use only Ford-approved coolant to minimize seal degradation. Consider extended warranty coverage when purchasing a high-mileage Flex.

decisions.reason: The article describes six individual coil packs, while the catalog evidence identifies a different coil-pack configuration; the existing claim must remain blocked pending content correction.

sourceEvidence.title: Ignition Coil Pack Failure
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace all six coil packs and spark plugs as a set for reliability. Use Motorcraft or quality aftermarket coils. Clear misfire codes after replacement.

decisions.reason: Cardone 20-323 matches the prescribed power-steering pump, is catalog-confirmed for every 2005-2007 article year without an application restriction, and its existing exact eBay product link remains valid.

sourceEvidence.title: Power Steering Pump Whine and Leak
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the power steering pump and flush the system. Inspect all hoses and the steering rack for leaks. Use Mercon V as the power steering fluid per Ford spec.

decisions.reason: MAHLE MS16296 carries VIN, package, location, and application restrictions that are absent from the unscoped claim.

sourceEvidence.title: 4.6L Plastic Intake Manifold Coolant Crossover Cracking and Coolant Leaks
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the intake manifold crossover and thermostat housing area for cracks or seepage. The durable fix is replacement with the updated Ford or Dorman intake manifold design that uses an improved aluminum crossover. If overheating occurred, inspect coils, plugs, and head gaskets before returning the car to service.

decisions.reason: Cardone 47-1755 is a front-left window motor, but the article and existing row do not preserve the side and position restriction.

sourceEvidence.title: Power Window Motor Burnout
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace the window motor. The regulator usually survives and can be reused. Lubricate the window tracks with white lithium grease to reduce motor strain.

decisions.reason: Aisin THRFD-0014 covers only a later/date-limited subset of the article, while the existing verified row is unscoped.

sourceEvidence.title: Plastic Thermostat Housing Cracks and Coolant Leaks on 2.3L Duratec
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the thermostat housing, sensor seals, and nearby hose connections for seepage or cracks. Replace the housing assembly, thermostat, and O-rings with updated parts, then refill and properly bleed the cooling system. If overheating occurred, verify fan operation and check for head-gasket damage afterward.

decisions.reason: Denso 471-0919 is limited to 2019-2021 2.5L vehicles without rear climate control, restrictions the unscoped public claim does not preserve.

sourceEvidence.title: A/C Compressor Failure or No-Cool Condition (Refrigerant Leak/Compressor Damage)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Recover and measure refrigerant, leak-test with dye/nitrogen, and repair leaking components (O-rings/lines/condenser as needed). If compressor has failed internally, replace the compressor, receiver/drier (or desiccant), and expansion device as applicable, then flush lines and evacuate/recharge to spec.

decisions.reason: Delphi SS20881 is a rear-position sensor while the article instructs diagnosis of the affected corner; the unscoped row can expose the wrong position.

sourceEvidence.title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor/Wiring Fault (ABS/Traction Control Lights On)
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Scan ABS module for wheel speed sensor DTCs and view live wheel speed data to identify the affected corner. Clean/inspect tone rings (if applicable), repair wiring/connectors, or replace the wheel speed sensor; clear codes and verify on a road test.

decisions.reason: MAHLE MIS16230-1 misses the article's 1999 endpoint and carries a VIN/application restriction that is absent from the unscoped claim.

sourceEvidence.title: Intake Manifold Gasket Coolant Leak
sourceEvidence.howToFix: Replace both upper and lower intake manifold gaskets. Use updated Fel-Pro gaskets. Flush the cooling system and change the oil if coolant contamination is found.
